findings.title: UsernameForm calls a passkeys method that does not exist
findings.body: UsernameForm.authenticate() now calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments so re-authentication will not skip the username form when passkeys are on. The only method added on UsernamePasswordForm is isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel); nothing in the authenticator hierarchy defines a no-arg overload, and there is no static import. This does not compile, so the services module cannot build and the username-form re-authentication change never runs. Call the real method (for example isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())) and make sure that implementation does not require a non-null user if it is also used before identity is known.

findings.title: Conditional passkeys UI is no longer set up on the initial login page
findings.body: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) is true only when its user argument is non-null, and both setup sites now use that helper: authenticate() around line 115 and the error challenge() override around line 137. Previously fillContextForm ran when passkeys were enabled and the user was not yet selected (context.getUser() == null). That is what puts the WebAuthn challenge, rpId, and AUTH_CHALLENGE_NOTE on the first login page and on the invalid-username error page. The new check is the inverse, so a normal login with no user on the context never embeds passkey data. Discoverable-credential sign-in and the username webauthn autocomplete field stop working, and passkey-only users (the existing tests delete the password before expecting auto-login) cannot authenticate. Unchanged tests such as webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey and the first page of passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey still require that form. Drop the user != null requirement so passkeys are prepared both before the user is known and during re-authentication; WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators() already returns false, so fillContextForm will not abort when a known user has no registered authenticators.
